question: Is there any hierarchy or priority among States under international law?
choices: Yes, the States that were the founding members of the United Nations are vested with more powers and authority

Whether there will be any hierarchy among States is a matter of each international organization to decide

subject: international_law
question: What is the obligation of the peaceful settlement of disputes?
choices: It is an obligation of result, that is, States are under a strict obligation to resolve their disputes as soon as possible
It is an obligation of conduct, ie States have an obligation to try to resolve their disputes through peaceful means. This does not entail an obligation to resolve their disputes
It is a peremptory norm of international law and all States have a legal interest to safeguard its application in any given dispute
It is an obligation which concerns solely international courts and tribunals
model_response: {"answer":"B","explanation":"The obligation of peaceful settlement of disputes is an obligation of conduct, which requires States to attempt to resolve their disputes through peaceful means.
